alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 3:52PM EST until November 2 at 6:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Central Brevard County in east central Florida...

* WHEN...Until 600 PM EST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Expect many
areas of slow moving or standing water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 352 PM EST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Flooding is already occurring in
the warned area. Between 6 and 10 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Melbourne, Titusville, Rockledge, Cocoa, Cocoa Beach, Satellite
Beach, Cape Canaveral, Indialantic, Sharpes, Merritt Island, Port
Saint John, Port Canaveral, Titusville Airport, Patrick Space
Force Base, Playalinda Beach, Mims, Indian Harbour Beach, Jetty
Park and Canaveral Groves.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 2:15PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
alerts.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused the St. Johns River near Cocoa to rise
into Minor Flood Stage. The river is forecast to rise through Minor
flood stage and into Moderate flood stage mid to late week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...From this afternoon until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 16.7 feet, Water covers yards, encroaches on homes and
may enter low lying homes along the St Johns River in the Lake
Poinsett area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:15 PM EST Monday the stage was 16.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:15 PM EST Monday was 16.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 16.8 feet early
Thursday afternoon. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 2 at 1:44PM EST until November 3 at 3:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
alerts.areas: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
alerts.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 6 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, and Coastal
Brevard Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 AM EST Tuesday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of east central Florida, including the following
areas, Indian River, Martin, Saint Lucie, Volusia, Okeechobee and
Brevard.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy to extreme rainfall has occurred over coastal portions of
east central Florida today. Any additional rainfall overnight may
exacerbate ongoing flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

advisories.text: Stay home and off the roadways unless necessary to travel to and from work or to escape high flooding. US 192 in Melbourne has flooded out. Expect significant delays.
Stay off the roads. Roads are flooded and cars are disabled throughout the city. Call 911 for life-or-death emergencies only.
Palm Bay City Hall and city offices closed today due to flooding. Widespread flooding in Palm Bay; avoid flooded roadways. Recreation facilities closed; trash collection cancelled today.
Never drive through standing water; stay indoors during the warning. No specific Cocoa Beach road closures posted.
Limit water use: rain plus normal use is stressing the wastewater system (Cocoa Beach lift stations at capacity).
All schools closed today due to flooding.

advisories.agency: Space Launch Delta 45 (Patrick SFB / Cape Canaveral SFS)
advisories.text: Non-mission-essential personnel should not report today because of hazardous roads and local flooding on base.

Wastewater system at capacity after overnight rain; controlled release of treated reclaimed water into the Indian River Lagoon began about 6:30 a.m. at the Osprey facility. Residents asked to cut nonessential water use (laundry, dishwashers, long showers) until further notice. Some Titusville streets impassable.
Routes 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 27, 28 and 30 (Melbourne and Palm Bay area) suspended for Monday because of flooding. Routes 26 and 29 running with long delays; long delays on all other routes.
Brevard County government facilities closed countywide today because of flooding; all courts also closed.
